newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Montoro says rates have not yet hit bottom.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Montoro says rates have not yet hit bottom.

text.p: Spain's Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Thursday that interest rates had not yet touched bottom and that the inflation rate in May would be below April's 1.7 percent.
"Spain still has an overly high risk premium and that means that we could defend an interest rate decline in long-rates, and with more intensity, in short rates.
"To speak of an interest rate floor doesn't respond to current economic reality," Montoro told journalists at a seminar on the euro.
Montoro also said that inflation should moderate from April's 1.7 percent CPI year-on-year rate.
"Everything suggests that the month of May we will fall even more from the 1.7 percent rate, Montoro said.
Montoro said that Spain was in a phase of economic growth and that "years of recovery and growth are coming."
